page: Microsoft Azure D8als_v6 is a general-purpose, compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The instance provisions 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores using hyperthreading, built on the x86_64 architecture. Memory allocation stands at 16.0 GB of RAM, corresponding to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying on external network-attached storage volumes, and does not feature dedicated GPU accelerators. Microsoft Hyper-V serves as the underlying virtualization layer.

Benchmark testing highlights notable single-core throughput, with the AMD processor recording 3079.88 on stress-ng single-core and 2102.0 on Geekbench single-core, both falling within the top 25% tier. Extended instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, and bfloat16 contribute to strong single-threaded text processing and small-scale language model inference generation. Multi-core operations register in the middle 50% distribution, reflecting standard hyperthreaded scaling. A measurable performance tradeoff appears in uncached memory access, where large-block read bandwidth drops into the bottom 25% at 38.06 GB/sec, even though cached small-block reads reach 607.81 GB/sec.

Because the D8als_v6 combines robust single-thread compute speeds with a constrained 2.0 GB per vCPU memory profile, it provides a cost-efficient resource tier for tasks where high per-core performance is prioritized over large RAM footprints. The absence of local disk drives necessitates consideration of remote storage bandwidth. This instance is suitable for web serving, microservices, batch processing, continuous integration pipelines, and lightweight computational jobs that do not demand extensive in-memory caches.
description: Microsoft Azure D8als_v6 is a virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a low-memory profile of 16.0 GB of RAM, it supplies 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage disks or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying instead on network-attached storage. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread compute capabilities, placing in the top quartile for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside support for AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions. However, memory-intensive operations encounter limitations, as large-block uncached read bandwidth drops into the lower quartile. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio provides a cost-efficient platform for compute-oriented tasks that do not require extensive memory footprints. D8als_v6 is well suited for web serving, continuous integration builds, microservices, and general compute workloads.
